items.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable and Mythos 5.1 for Advanced Coding and Research
items.summary: Anthropic has rolled out two new frontier AI models, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, positioning them as the most capable systems yet for software development, enterprise knowledge work, and scientific research. While both models share identical underlying architecture, they differ in one key respect: the strength of their safeguards. Fable 5.1 is generally available to all users, whereas Mythos 5.1 is restricted to vetted professionals through Anthropic’s trusted access programs, with permissions tailored specifically for cybersecurity defenders and life sciences researchers. The release addresses three recurring pain points enterprise customers have raised about earlier Claude models: cost, data privacy, and overly aggressive content safeguards. On pricing, Anthropic says Fable 5.1 will run roughly 25 percent cheaper than Fable 5 for typical workloads, and up to 45 percent cheaper for heavily agentic tasks, largely due to a 75 percent price cut on cached input reads, now $0.25 per million tokens. Input and output token pricing otherwise remains unchanged at $10 and $50 per million tokens, respectively. Claude Fable and Mythos 5.1 Data handling gets a significant overhaul through Anthropic’s new Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) framework, which lets organizations store their data entirely within their own cloud infrastructure rather than on Anthropic’s servers, delivering zero-data-retention-level privacy while still catching adversarial misuse. EFS will roll out in phases starting this fall across Claude Code, Claude Enterprise, the Claude Platform, and major cloud partners including AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. Until then, eligible enterprise customers can already use Fable 5.1 under a zero-retention policy. On the safeguards front, Anthropic reports a 60 percent drop in false-positive interventions for cybersecurity-related queries, partly because Fable 5.1 is now permitted to identify software vulnerabilities for defensive purposes, though it still cannot generate exploits. Higher-risk dual-use tasks such as penetration testing and binary vulnerability scanning are automatically redirected to Anthropic’s Opus-class models instead. Anthropic’s internal testing shows Fable 5.1 outperforming its predecessor across coding, agentic reasoning, and knowledge-work benchmarks, including Terminal-Bench 4.0, GDPval-AA v2, and Humanity’s Last Exam. Early enterprise partners including Jane Street, Cognition, MongoDB, Datadog, and Millennium reported the model solving problems that had stumped engineering teams for years, including a rare production crash that had eluded human debuggers for nearly five years. Mythos 5.1’s research capabilities extend into scientific domains. In molecular biology testing, the model designed high-affinity protein binders that outperformed leading entries in Adaptyv Bio’s design competitions, achieving nearly a 50 percent hit rate against a typical industry benchmark of 10 to 15 percent. Separately, Fable 5.1 built a new high-resolution elevation map of Venus using decades-old NASA Magellan radar data, ahead of upcoming ESA and NASA missions. Mythos 5.1’s advanced biology and cybersecurity capabilities remain gated behind Anthropic’s Cyber Verification Program and Life Sciences Verification Program, developed in coordination with the US government, with plans to broaden eligibility over time. Anthropic has also confirmed compliance with the EU AI Act’s Code of Practice, embedding invisible watermarking into outputs from models released after August 2, 2026, alongside a detection API now in private preview for regulators and researchers. Fable 5.1 is available immediately on Claude’s platforms and via the API under the identifier claude-fable-5-1. Prevent incidents due to slow investigations. items.title: OWASP Launches OASIS AI Initiative to Fix Open Source Vulnerabilities at Scale
items.summary: OWASP has launched the Open Automated Security Initiative for Software (OASIS), a global community effort designed to close the gap between finding vulnerabilities in open source code and actually fixing them. Announced on August 26, 2026, in San Francisco, the initiative pairs AI-generated fix candidates with human validation from application security professionals, aiming to deliver credible, ready-to-use patches to open source maintainers instead of just longer vulnerability lists. Open source software underlies roughly 98% of commercial codebases, according to the Black Duck 2026 Open Source Security and Risk Analysis Report, yet maintainers are routinely overwhelmed by scanning tools that flag issues without offering usable remediation paths. OASIS addresses that bottleneck through a three-stage process. Automated tooling first scans widely used repositories and generates candidate fixes as vulnerabilities surface. A community of AppSec practitioners and agents then reviews each candidate for correctness and safety, cutting validation time down to minutes. Finally, vetted patches are submitted upstream, giving maintainers a trustworthy starting point they can adapt to their own codebase rather than a raw AI suggestion, complementing modern open-source vulnerability scanner workflows. Since opening early sign-ups, OASIS has drawn hundreds of application security professionals across industries, backed by founding sponsors AppSecAI, Intigriti, and DryRun Security. As detailed in the OWASP OASIS announcement , Chris Holt, Strategic Engagement and Community Architect at Intigriti, said open source underpins the majority of the information economy, making unremediated vulnerabilities a systemic risk, and that OASIS lets the AppSec and open source communities cooperatively deliver secure software together. The timing reflects a shifting threat landscape. Attackers are increasingly using “vibe hacking,” AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation that outpaces manual defense. James Wickett, CEO of DryRun Security, noted that the same generative AI accelerating attacks can accelerate defense when paired with independent validation and community expertise. Michael Cartsonis of AppSecAI added that OASIS finally gives security professionals with code-review experience a fast, low-friction way to contribute. Stage / Component Process & Operational Model Strategic Impact Automated Scanning & Generation AI-driven tooling scans repos and crafts patch candidates Accelerates initial remediation proposals for newly found CVEs AppSec Community Validation Human-in-the-loop expert review and agent validation Cuts review cycles to minutes and eliminates false-positive fixes Upstream Submission Delivery of vetted, ready-to-merge patches to maintainers Reduces maintainer burden with production-grade remediation Ecosystem Collaboration Vendor-neutral backing (OWASP, Intigriti, DryRun Security) Secures long-tail open source dependencies across commercial stacks OASIS is positioned as a complement to enterprise-led efforts such as OpenAI’s Patch the Planet, the Linux Foundation’s Akrites, and Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, which focus elite research teams on high-priority infrastructure like operating systems and browsers. OASIS instead scales through volunteer AppSec crowds to cover the long tail of libraries and applications enterprises actually run, an approach David Kosorok, Director of Product Security at ACV Auctions, called the highest-leverage work in application security, since one validated upstream fix can secure thousands of downstream applications simultaneously, bolstering defense against offensive vulnerability discovery tool automation. Participation is open through several roles, including vulnerability validators, repo community managers, maintainer liaisons, and automation operators, making OASIS a vendor-neutral entry point for security practitioners wanting to help fix, not just find, the vulnerabilities threatening the open source software that powers modern infrastructure.
